IS : 7845 - 1975

Indian Standard
METHOD FOR EVALUATING STRENGTH OF REACTIVE DYES ( TRICHLOROPYRIMIDYL TYPE ) BY DYEING TEST
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 11 November 1975, after the draft finalized by the Dyestuffs Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. The method laid 0.2 Reactive dyes are marketed in different strengths. down in this standard for determining the strength of trichloropyrimidyl type ( reactone/drimarene ) dyestuffs against a mutually accepted standard would be useful for assessing the comparative strength of dyestuffs only. This method may not necessarily be the most economical method of dyeing. 0.3 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes a method for determination reactive dyes ( trichloropyrimidyl type ) by dyeing test. 2. SAMPLING 2.1 Lot - All the containers of the same dye and of the same concentration delivered to a buyer against a despatch note shall constitute a lot. 2.2 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer and the seller, the number of containers to be selected at random from a lot shall be as given helow:

2.3 From each container draw small quantities of dye from at least 3 different parts by a suitable sampling instrument and mix them thoroughly to get a composite sample weighing about 20 g. This shall constitute the test sample. 3. STANDARD

5.3 Compare the dyeings as obtained in 5.2 and the dyeings obtained -as in 5.1 ( see Note ). Select a dyeing ofthe dyestuff under test which exactly matches with one of the dyeings of the standard dyestuff. Note the percentage of the dyeing which matches exactly.
NOTE -&fore comparing the dyeings, they shall be spread out properly. The dried hanks shall be laid side by side in the same plane and oriented in the same direction. They shall be combed to a uniform thickness to avoid the effects of backing on the appearance. The hanks shall be compared, if possible, in north skylight. The consistency in strength variation of different dyeings of standard dyestuff and the If the strength variations between the two dyestuff under test shall be observed. consecutive dyeings are not constant, the dyeings shall be repeated.
